ranking.why: The patient fact of ventricular fibrillation and the reference material stating that polymorphic ventricular tachycardia can degenerate into ventricular fibrillation support this diagnosis.
The patient fact of QTc interval of 380 ms and the reference material stating that a normal QTc in men is less than 440ms support this diagnosis.

The patient fact of ejection fraction of 47.5% and the reference material stating that hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is characterized by left ventricle hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of absence of Brugada pattern on ECG and the reference material stating that Brugada syndrome is characterized by idiopathic ventricular fibrillation in association with right ventricular electrocardiogram abnormalities rule out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of normal cardiovascular examination and the reference material stating that cardiomyopathy can cause cardiac syncope do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of normal wall thickness and the reference material stating that arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy can be identified pathologically by the replacement of myocytes within the right ventricle with fibrous tissue and fat cells do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.
The patient fact of risperidone treatment and the lack of reference material for this condition do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of autism spectrum disorder and the reference material stating that cardiovascular syncope will more commonly be associated with exertion do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of normal chemistry panel and the reference material stating that metabolic syndrome is associated with accelerated atherosclerosis do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of normal ECG and the reference material stating that an abnormal ECG at rest raises suspicions of a concealed form of cardiomyopathy or a channelopathy do not provide enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.
The patient fact of absence of seizure history and the reference material stating that seizures occur in up to 1.4% of term infants rule out this diagnosis.
